segments: Verification scope: nixpkgs nixos-unstable modules and upstream documentation consulted in October 2026. Group lists, package counts, and service defaults change with each revision. For deployment, use the nixpkgs and Home Manager source locked by your project as the authority. No builds, activation, or desktop runtime tests were performed for this article.

Authoritative module sources: nixos/modules/services/desktop-managers/gnome.nix (the main module) and nixos/modules/services/desktops/gnome/*.nix (service switches). The accompanying official gnome.md documentation is in the same directory as the main module. This reference lists the main public interfaces under services.desktopManager.gnome.*, services.gnome.*, and environment.gnome.*, together with the service switches available at the time and their defaults. “Automatically enabled by GNOME” indicates the service switch's actual effective default; changing it manually may break the desktop.

How extraGSettingsOverrides Works The main module combines extraGSettingsOverrides, extraGSettingsOverridePackages, and favoriteAppsOverride into the pkgs.gnome.nixos-gsettings-overrides package, generates share/gsettings-schemas/nixos-gsettings-overrides/glib-2.0/schemas/, and injects it into the session through the NIX_GSETTINGS_OVERRIDES_DIR environment variable. This is therefore the “system defaults” layer; existing user dconf values take precedence. See Managing GSettings and dconf on NixOS.

Default Structure of the Group Switches core-os-services and core-shell are assigned true at normal priority, inside the main module's lib.mkIf with a direct = true assignment. Disabling them dismantles the desktop. core-apps uses mkDefault true, which users can override with = false for a minimal GNOME setup. games/dev-tools default to false and are installed only when enabled. See Declarative GNOME Management.

Disabling Services Removes Functionality The official documentation explicitly states that disabling these services is unsupported and may break applications. A classic example: disabling both tinysparql and localsearch removes GNOME search; GNOME Music will not work without TinySPARQL.
Removed: gnome-online-miners (mkRemovedOptionModule, broken for a while now).
4. Package Exclusion: environment.gnome.excludePackages

Type: listOf package, default: []. Matches by package name to remove packages from environment.systemPackages in core-apps / games / core-developer-tools (the main module's removeExcluded/notExcluded)

Primarily intended to exclude packages from these three groups; the actual source also filters core-shell's optionalPackages. Most core-shell packages are mandatory; only optionalPackages can be excluded. Excluding Epiphany usually also removes the large webkitgtk package from the system closure

Excluding a package also skips the corresponding program module. For example, excluding sushi prevents the sushi service from being enabled; excluding gnome-disk-utility prevents programs.gnome-disks from being enabled
5. What Each Group Installs by Default

core-apps (25): baobab, decibels, epiphany, gnome-text-editor, gnome-calculator, gnome-calendar, gnome-characters, gnome-clocks, gnome-console, gnome-contacts, gnome-font-viewer, gnome-logs, gnome-maps, gnome-music, gnome-system-monitor, gnome-tecla, gnome-weather, loupe, nautilus, papers, gnome-connections, showtime, simple-scan, snapshot, yelp.

games (20): aisleriot, atomix, five-or-more, four-in-a-row, gnome-2048, gnome-chess, gnome-klotski, gnome-mahjongg, gnome-mines, gnome-nibbles, gnome-robots, gnome-sudoku, gnome-taquin, gnome-tetravex, hitori, iagno, lightsoff, quadrapassel, swell-foop, tali.
core-developer-tools (5): dconf-editor, devhelp, d-spy, gnome-builder, sysprof.

Some excludable optional packages in core-shell (consult your locked source): adwaita-icon-theme, gnome-backgrounds, gnome-bluetooth, gnome-color-manager, gnome-control-center, gnome-tour, gnome-user-docs, gnome-menus, xdg-user-dirs, xdg-user-dirs-gtk.

Adding Packages vs. Removing Packages To install more GNOME ecosystem packages, such as pkgs.gpaste or pkgs.gnomeExtensions.*, add them directly to environment.systemPackages. To install fewer, use excludePackages. NixOS has no dedicated option to “add custom packages through GNOME”: the group lists are hardcoded, so custom additions go through systemPackages.
